_comment: invent.c sortloot() and sortloot_cmp(): loot_classify() runs lazily inside the comparator and, when the hero can see, marks each object encountered (o_init.c observe_object()), so the order of discoveries within a class follows the order in which the C library's qsort() first compares the objects (nethack-c/patches/002-deterministic-qsort.patch). macOS and glibc call the comparator in different orders, so record this recipe on macOS (.github/workflows/macos-recorder.yml), not with a Linux recorder; see docs/testing.md, "The qsort() call order". Armor and amulets are created with dknown set (mkobj.c clear_dknown()), so invent.c learn_unseen_invent() skips them when the blindfold comes off and the inventory sort is the first to observe them. A blindfolded Monk wishes for two rings, two amulets and three gems, takes the blindfold off, lists his inventory (invent.c display_pickinv(), seventeen objects) and pages through his discoveries.
